description:
The verify-fast-duration gate normalizes each run by a single-threaded CPU loop (`calibration_best_seconds`), which does not predict fast-tier time: tests run on 4 xdist workers under coverage. Runner classes therefore carry fixed offsets (median shared ratio about 1.18 for factor < 0.99, about 1.0 for factor 1.35-1.39, about 1.22 for factor > 1.6), the same commit scores 1.01-1.29 on different runners, and the bias is present on the day a baseline is built. The baseline is also built low (sum of per-test p50s / median source-run sum = 0.94) and samples only CI runs that concluded success. New-test time is charged for every id absent from the baseline, so PRs pay for tests other PRs added.

Work:
1. Normalize by the run's recorded `collection.max_seconds` (or a 4-process calibration if that proves better), and record it for every baseline source run.
2. Rescale the baseline so its shared sum matches the median source run; select source runs by complete fast-junit and calibration artifacts rather than CI conclusion, excluding runs whose tests failed.
3. Charge new-test excess only for ids in test files the PR itself changes.
4. `scripts/pr_rerun.py` must not call a would-block 'a real slowdown, not runner noise' when the same head has a passing verdict on another run.

Guardrails: owner decision 2026-11-17 stands (no threshold changes; 1.30 and 360 s stay, block mode stays). Never weaken the gate for a PR that really slows the tier.
